current_evidence: It is the top official result for Oldham's validation checklist and cites Places for Everyone (adopted 2024) and the 2024 BNG regulations, so it supersedes the older checklist (download id 2785); the document itself states no adoption or publication date, and the shared fetch budget ran out before the 'apply for planning permission' page (download 781) that links it could be read.

issues.detail: The List date of 2025-10-01 comes from PDF metadata (CreationDate). The checklist text gives no adoption, publication or version date, so the date cannot be confirmed from the document.
issues.evidence: Date basis = 'PDF metadata CreationDate'; the document title 'Oldham Council – Planning Validation Checklist' carries no date or version.

issues.detail: Grokbot missed about 13 local requirements that the checklist sets out with clear criteria: (1) Affordable Housing Statement – major residential; (2) Air Quality Statement – major development in an AQMA, residential over 50 dwellings, major over 5,000 sqm, combustion uses (power stations, biomass, incineration), or over 50 car parking spaces; (3) Archaeological Impact Assessment – conversion or change of use of former textile mills, or substantial demolition, excavation or new build in their curtilage, and demolition, excavation or new buildings in a Conservation Area or the curtilage of a listed building; (4) Contaminated Land Survey (Phase I, and Phase II if needed) – major development, minor new-build residential, schools or hospitals, and changes of use to those uses on previously industrial land; (5) Crime Impact Statement – residential of 50+ units, office or commercial over 2,500 sqm, all new student accommodation, retail, hotel, health, leisure or worship uses over 2,500 sqm, and transport stations of 1,000 sqm+; (6) Employment & Skills Statement – major schemes of 100+ dwellings or 2,500 sqm+ of commercial floorspace, including mixed use that exceeds these together; (7) Landscape Visual Impact Assessment – major development in the Green Belt or Other Protected Open Land, or with significant landscape or townscape impact; (8) Levels / Sections – major and minor new buildings or extensions, and uneven sites including house extensions (rear extensions to terraced houses excepted); (9) Lighting Impact Assessment – communal external areas over 50 sqm or parking for 4+ vehicles, outdoor sport and recreation, floodlighting, and development within 10m of a Main River, open water, SSSI or SBI; (10) Open Space, Sports and Recreation Statement – all major development, and minor development that loses open space or sports facilities; (11) Planning Statement – all major development; (12) Sustainability, Carbon and Energy Statement – all major and minor development creating new floorspace, and changes of use creating new dwellings; (13) Infrastructure phasing and delivery strategy – sites that are phased or developed by more than one developer (this text sits beside the Telecommunications row). Most of these also apply to Outline and Reserved matters, which Grokbot marks '(none)'.
issues.evidence: Checklist table items 'Affordable Housing Statement', 'Air Quality Statement', 'Archaeological Impact Assessment', 'Contaminated Land Survey', 'Crime Impact Statement', 'Employment & Skills Statement', 'Landscape Visual Impact Assessment', 'Levels / Sections', 'Lighting Impact Assessment', 'Open Space, Sports, and Recreation Statement', 'Planning Statement', 'Sustainability, Carbon and Energy Statement'.

issues.detail: Householder is marked '(none)', but the source applies local requirements to householder work: a Heritage Statement for development in a Conservation Area 'including house extensions', Levels/Sections for house extensions on uneven sites, and Tree Surveys where trees with a stem over 75mm may be affected. Outline and Reserved matters are also marked '(none)', although the major-development thresholds (FRA, Coal Mining, SuDS, Transport, DAS, Planning Statement and others) apply to them.
issues.evidence: Heritage Statement: 'All development proposed within a Conservation Area (including house extensions and partial or total demolition)'; Levels/Sections: applies to 'house extensions' on uneven sites.

issues.detail: Twenty Full-planning rows carry 'INFERRED: application type not named ... placed under Full planning'. The checklist is a general list for all planning applications, and many items name thresholds (Major/Minor) rather than application types. Examples: Arboricultural, Ecological Survey, Noise, Viability and Transport were all guessed. The Design and Access Statement appears only under Listed building consent, but the source also requires it for all Major development and for dwellings or 100 sqm+ in a Conservation Area. Biodiversity Net Gain was placed under Full planning without noting the householder exemption.
issues.evidence: DAS criteria: 'All Major developments; ... designated area ... one or more dwellings ... or 100 sqm or more; Listed Building Consent applications'.

issues.detail: 'Retail / Town Centre Impact Assessment / Sequential test' is placed under 'Change of use - prior approval'. Its excerpt merges the Telecommunications row, whose Part 16 prior notification wording caused the misplacement. The source applies the town centre test to main town centre uses outside centres, not to prior approvals. Telecommunications is also shown only under prior approval, although it applies to all telecoms proposals, including full applications.
issues.evidence: 'Town Centre Uses – Sequential': main town centre uses outside centres and not in accordance with the Local Plan; Impact Assessment for retail or leisure over 2,500 sqm.

issues.detail: Several triggers are text taken from another item. 'Highways / access details (visibility splays)', 'Schedule of works (listed building)' and 'Viability Assessment' all quote the Tree Survey criteria about 75mm stem diameter. The checklist has no Highways/visibility-splay item and no listed-building Schedule of Works item. The real Viability trigger is where the applicant claims the scheme cannot meet policy requirements and agrees to fund independent review.
issues.evidence: Grokbot Viability excerpt: 'Method Statements Viability Assessment ... stem diameter greater than 75 mm ...'; source Viability criteria: applicant claims scheme cannot meet policy requirements.

issues.detail: Several triggers are cut off or garbled. Ecological Survey reads only 'to support protected species.'; the real triggers are all Major development, demolition of buildings that could support protected species, minor development within or near (50m) an SSSI or SBI, and minor development within 10m of a canal, green corridor or Flood Zone 2/3. Travel Plan reads only 'to provide a Travel Plan.' Noise quotes the opt-out wording instead of the triggers (noise-generating B2/B8 uses, sensitive uses near noise sources, evening-economy uses, schools and hospitals). The FRA excerpt is split mid-sentence ('Policy 2, 3 and 3b') and leaves out sites over 1 ha, surface-water flood areas where a more vulnerable use is introduced, and Flood Zone 1 sites at increased risk in the SFRA. The Housing mix/NDSS excerpt is page-header debris that drops the trigger (all new residential, including conversions, HMOs and student accommodation). The Heritage Statement excerpt runs into the Health Impact Assessment text.
issues.evidence: Ecological Assessment criteria: 'All Major ... demolition of buildings that could support protected species ... within 50m of SSSI/SBI ... within 10m of a canal, green corridor or Flood Zones 2 and 3'.

issues.detail: 'Photographs / Photomontages' and 'Self-build / custom build information' are not local requirements in this checklist. The photographs excerpt is the file-format rule that supporting documents must be PDFs. The self-build excerpt is the Biodiversity Net Gain exemption criteria.
issues.evidence: 'letters, reports, photographs etc.) must be submitted in PDF format'; 'Self-build and custom build applications - You must meet all of the following conditions to qualify for an exemption'.

issues.detail: Several tab items are process text or fragments, not requirements: the 10-working-day invalid-notice statement; a fragment combining the GM habitat bank guidance link with national Ownership Certificate text; and three 'Policy-driven requirements' entries that are page-break debris. One is headed 'Sustainability, Carbon and Energy Statement' but contains the JP-G5 South Pennines SAC policy text; another ends mid-sentence ('You need to include a sustainable drainage strategy if your application is for:').
issues.evidence: 'Where a decision is made to declare an application invalid the Council will write to the agent ... within 10 working days.'

issues.detail: The drawing-standards items are split into fragments with list markers and page headers ('i) ii) iii) iv) v) vi) Site address/name;', 'Paper size. d) ...', 'Oldham Council – Planning Validation Checklist h) ...'). As a result, the title-box contents (site address, drawing reference, title, scale, date, paper size) cannot be read as one requirement.
issues.evidence: Section 2 'Plans/Drawings' c) 'Each drawing to contain a Title Box including: i)-vi)'.

summary: Grokbot's link works and appears to be Oldham's current checklist, but its date comes only from PDF metadata. The extraction misses about 13 local requirements, including Affordable Housing, Air Quality, Contaminated Land, Planning Statement, Lighting, Levels and Sustainability, wrongly marks Householder/Outline/RM as having no local requirements, and has several triggers copied from the tree-survey row.
